title: [CQ-I05] VS Code managed VM interface
description:
Objective: Mirror primary VM lifecycle/readiness/recovery behavior.

Deliverable: VS Code managed VM interface. This is task I05 of the approved full CQ rollout; consume this contract, not the whole reference document.

Scope boundaries: implement this behavior and its regression tests only. Later activation, other platform/client consumers and other task behaviors remain out of scope unless named here. Approved full CQ-01–CQ-08 rollout from the interactive implementation plan (2026-10-24). CQ-01 is already landed. Use original Moe source; daemon owns state, wrappers own host Git writes. User selected Moe-provisioned LOCAL Linux VMs (not cloud CI), coding/QA and checks isolated, and exact designated LOCAL BRANCH delivery. Strong profile stays disabled until isolation, evidence and client gates pass. Preserve legacy behavior and existing dirty bytes. Never directly edit .moe. No second revision authority, scheduler, graph database or native memory database.

Dependency aliases (wired by Moe task ids after import): I04, I03.

The module loads with a throwing require, which pins purity (no vscode import). Run: managed-vm fails with ENOENT on src/util/ManagedVm.ts (the expected red). settings-wire: harness now also passes `client` to the body (a one-line change). New S6 (DoD 3) ALREADY PASSES, as the plan allowed: the client stores the raw SETTINGS_UPDATED payload. It is kept as the pin. Comparison uses JSON.stringify because the client parses in its own vm realm. Baseline before this step: 165/165 pass. Peer-dirty moe-vscode/scripts/bundle-assets.mjs left untouched.

GREEN. src/util/ManagedVm.ts is pure (the test's throwing require proves it imports nothing).

Exports:
- decode(command, stdout, exit, timedOut), readiness, strongProfile, rows, actions, notes, commandArgs, runVmControl, unreadable, TIMEOUT_MS.
- Field checks run in the same order as I03's ManagedVmPresentation.parse, so a multi-defect report gets the same verdict on both clients (for the I06b corpus).

Behaviour:
- Unreadable reasons: timed-out, failed, too-large, malformed, not-owned, cancelled, node-missing, script-missing, no-project. Texts reuse the JetBrains MoeBundle wording.
- Codes and reasons resolve through a Map, so the token 'constructor' is not looked up on the prototype (tested in V4).
- runVmControl(execFileImpl, node, script, command, root, signal?): the timeout comes from TIMEOUT_MS[command] (120 s, or 20 min for cleanup), and signal is added only when given.
  - AbortError gives cancelled, MAXBUFFER gives too-large, ENOENT gives node-missing.
  - Any other error never parses stdout.
  - A synchronous throw gives failed.

Runs: managed-vm 9/9 pass, `npx tsc -p ./ --noEmit` exit 0.

Wired the native TreeView.
- NEW src/providers/ManagedVmTreeProvider.ts, the moe.managedVms view. Roots:
  - 3 readiness lines;
  - the strong-profile line;
  - 'Profile: <executionProfile|legacy> · Delivery: <deliveryPolicy|legacy>', read-only, from client.currentState;
  - 'Owned VMs (n)' with its rows;
  - the notes for the last status and last action.
- run() is single flight and re-checks actions():
  - withProgress: a view progress bar for status and reconcile; a cancellable Notification for cleanup, whose cancel aborts the AbortController;
  - .catch gives unreadable('failed'); a refresh follows reconcile and cleanup.
- cleanup() asks a modal confirm, worded as in JB moe.managedVm.cleanup.confirm.
- execute() checks:
  - no workspace gives no-project;
  - a missing bundled/scripts/local-runner/vm-control.mjs gives script-missing (no process);
  - otherwise runVmControl(execFile, client.resolveDaemonRuntime().node, …).
- dispose() aborts the run and disposes the emitter and subscription.
- setContext moe.managedVms.canReconcile/canCleanup drives command enablement.

Other files:

- package.json: the view, 3 commands (icons; reconcile/cleanup enablement) and 3 view/title entries. There is no settings/profile command.
- MoeDaemonClient: `private` dropped from resolveDaemonRuntime only.

comments.content:
Parity note from the CQ-I06 planner (2026-10-30), for the CQ-I05 worker. CQ-I06b will run ONE shared corpus, moe-jetbrains/src/test/resources/client-verdicts.json, through both moe-jetbrains ManagedVmPresentation and your src/util/ManagedVm.ts. Your approved plan says "mirror I03". These are the landed I03 rules (ManagedVmPresentation.kt) where your plan text could drift. Matching them now avoids a fix-forward later:
1. decode is bound to the invoked command. A status run accepts only schema moe-vm-status-v1, reconcile only -reconcile-v1, cleanup only -cleanup-v1. A mismatch is Unreadable(malformed). So decode needs the command, or runVmControl must check the schema.
2. A well-formed report that carries a top-level "code" (e.g. {"schema":"moe-vm-status-v1","code":"LEDGER_UNREADABLE",...}) is Refused(code). It is not a Status, and not Unreadable.
3. rows() hides the phases 'collision' (a foreign VM that held the name) and 'deleted'.
4. Every instance name anywhere in the report must match ^moe-vm-[0-9a-f]{20}$ and appear once. A foreign or repeated name makes the whole report Unreadable(not-owned).
5. Cleanup is offered only when the provider is ready, nothing is running, and at least one visible row is in a LAUNCHED phase (launching|owned|absent|failed). One instance is not enough on its own: a 'reserved' row must not enable cleanup.
6. Only a literal JSON true counts for executionReady or verified. The strong-profile line is always blocked.
7. Unreadable has distinct reasons: timed-out, failed (nonzero exit), too-large (over 64 KiB), malformed and not-owned.
Please keep decode, readiness, rows and actions as exported pure functions, so the corpus test can call them directly.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
- A webview panel like SettingsPanel: rejected. It needs HTML, a media script and a CSP, which is more code and opens an HTML-injection surface. A native TreeView with view/title commands is the VS Code idiom, and it is smaller.
- Calling Multipass or reading a ledger from the extension: rejected, exactly as for I03. The CQ-I03a producer is the only ownership authority.
- Adding profile fields to the typed ProjectSettings: not needed. The client stores the daemon's raw project payload on SETTINGS_UPDATED (MoeDaemonClient about line 988), and SettingsPanel sends only six form keys. DoD 3 is pinned by a roundtrip test instead of a type change.
planningNotes.risks:
- Size: QA rejects past 400 net, and tests count. Use the per-file budget in step 4.
- Plan-size floor: 7 files makes this heavy, so the routing is opus.
- The producer may land different names or codes. Adapt, and keep the fail-closed decoder.
- Node < 22 makes the producer's cleanup preserve everything (DAEMON_UNREACHABLE). Render that as a normal report.
- No VS Code host or VM certification: headless tests only.
- CI wiring of the producer test is owed by I06 (comment on I06).
